name: Wealden

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme, and the council says it has no plans for one.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme; only national mandatory HMO licensing applies (five or more people from two or more households sharing facilities).

housing: Wealden is a large, rural district stretching from the coast at Pevensey Bay to the High Weald, and most homes are owner-occupied. Its towns, Hailsham, Uckfield, Crowborough and Heathfield, have grown with large new-build estates around older centres. Villages have tile-hung and weatherboarded cottages, farmhouses and barn conversions, many off the gas network. Bungalows are common in Polegate, Willingdon and along the coast, where many retired people live.
checkinTips: Rural cottages off the gas network: record the oil tank or LPG level, boiler type and any septic tank or private drainage.
Tile-hung and weatherboarded cottages in the High Weald: photograph cladding, timber windows, low beams and any damp patches.
Wood burners and open fires in village homes: note the sweep certificate date and the condition of hearths and stoves.
Coastal bungalows at Pevensey Bay: photograph window frames, door locks and any salt corrosion on metalwork and outdoor fittings.
New-build estates in Hailsham and Uckfield: check sealant, flooring and any snagging marks, and note who maintains shared areas.
Large gardens and driveways: photograph lawns, hedges, gates and outbuildings, as gardens often form part of the tenancy.
tenantHelp: Wealden District Council's Private Housing team advises private tenants and can look into disrepair and unsafe conditions in rented homes.
